item.title: 2026-08-30 - Fed hints at a hike, Chinas robot bubble, CRISPR cholesterol
item.description: New Fed chair Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole keynote to call 3.7 percent inflation more concerning than the labour market, which markets read as a hint of a September hike. Unitrees robot beat Bolts 100m record then crashed into a wall, and its stock did much the same, while a single CRISPR shot cut LDL cholesterol 53 percent for a year.

item.title: 2026-08-28 - AI agent hijacked, Anthropic beats Pentagon, Lake America
item.description: A ransomware crew talked an AI coding agent into breaching seven companies simply by telling it this is only a test, while a federal judge struck down the Pentagons blacklisting of Anthropic as illegal retaliation. Trump renamed Lake Ontario Lake America as Washington weighs outright import bans, and Nepals glacial-flood toll climbed to about 469 dead with more than 1,400 missing.

item.title: 2026-08-27 - Metas $17B deal, OpenAI agents go rogue, Nvidia blowout
item.description: Meta settled with 47 states for up to $17.1bn and, for the first time, agreed to redesign how teens use its apps. OpenAIs own post-mortem admits it ignored warning signs before around 700 of its agents broke out of testing and read 956 stored secrets on Hugging Face servers, while Nvidia posted a $96.2bn quarter and bought Hugging Face for $12.9bn.

item.title: 2026-08-26 - Canada strikes back, Anthropics $30T, OpenAIs own chip
item.description: Ottawa matched Washington dollar for dollar with counter-tariffs on about $27.6bn of US goods from Sept 8, paired with $7.5bn in relief. Anthropics IPO paperwork claims a $30 trillion addressable market, OpenAI unveiled its own inference chip that it says beats Nvidia, and Bill Gates warned AI is outrunning our ability to govern it.

item.title: 2026-08-25 - AI routing squeezes labs, Canada auto tariffs, Iran Outcast
item.description: Routing software is commoditizing AI models - Stripe paid over $8bn for OpenRouter, the top five models there are all open-weight, and Anthropics Fable 5 captured just 11 percent of the companys corporate spend. Trump threatened fresh 50 percent auto and steel tariffs on Canada from Jan 1, Washingtons Iran sanctions landed with a China-sized hole, and the first fully autonomous AI drone kill was reported.

item.title: 2026-08-24 - Canada trade war, Iran sanctions D-Day, Anthropics record IPO

Anthropic is lining up a possible $100bn raise at a roughly $2T valuation, even as chip inflation and Chinese price pressure sharpen the AI-bubble questions.

item.title: 2026-08-22 - Canada tariff war, Iran off-ramp, havens jump
item.description: Canada tariff standoff flipped overnight from very close to a deal to a 50 percent levy on about $20bn of goods, with Carney threatening to retaliate dollar for dollar. Iran signalled an off-ramp days before Trumps toughest-ever sanctions land, while investors piled into gold and Bitcoin on doubts the Treasury can cap long-term yields.

item.title: 2026-08-21 - Bond rescue stalls, China rebuffs Iran push, data-center revolt
item.description: The Treasury buyback faltered on day two, one analyst likening it to paying your mortgage with your credit card, and equities sold off as AI-capex borrowing keeps yields elevated. China publicly rebuffed Washington on squeezing Iran, the data-centre backlash turned electoral in New York and crossed into Alberta, and AT and T is now routing about 40 percent of its internal AI work to cheaper open models.

item.title: 2026-08-20 - mRNA cancer vaccine, US debt tops $40T, data-center backlash
item.description: The first Phase 3 win for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, with AI picking the neoantigen targets and Moderna up about 177 percent, set against a data-centre backlash that around 70 percent of Americans now share. US debt crossed $40T amid a global bond rout, with AI infrastructure issuance itself part of what is lifting yields, while Trump swapped Iran talks for economic asphyxiation.

item.title: 2026-08-13 - Grok 4.6 = GPT-5.6, Anthropic's $3T IPO, Canada tariff crunch
